newsitem.title: INDIA: India's United Front leader goes to meet president.
newsitem.headline: India's United Front leader goes to meet president.

text.p: Chandrababu Naidu, a leader of India's ruling United Front coalition and chief minister of Andhra Pradesh state, said on Friday that he was going to meet President Shankar Dayal Sharma.

"I'm going to brief the president about the current political situation," Naidu told reporters as he left a government guest house to see Sharma. Naidu is considered a possible candidate to replace Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda, who faced likely defeat in a vote of confidence.

The lower house of parliament was debating the confidence motion as Naidu left to see the president, who under India's constitution would name the next prime minister if Deve Gowda lost the vote or resigned.

The Congress party and the Bharatiya Janata Party, which between them control 333 votes in the 542-member house, had both vowed to vote against Deve Gowda, whose United Front alliance has 178 deputies. House speaker P.A. Sangma said Deve Gowda would reply to the confidence debate at 1530 GMT.
United Front and Congress leaders met informally throughout Friday to try to avert mid-term elections by finding a successor to Deve Gowda.

Naidu and G.K. Moopanar, a former Congress member from the southern state of Tamil Nadu who broke away last year, were considered the leading United Front candidates to replace Deve Gowda. Moopanar had met the president on Thursday.
